cues.zh: 那场崩溃之后的复苏，靠的是任天堂

cues.en: move of of controlling
cues.zh: 通过控制

cues.en: platforms

cues.en: to restore the industry has now become a problem and is happening again now in the social space. I wondered what you thought about these two things.

cues.en: Well, for those of you who weren't even alive then, the video game business crashed in 1983.
cues.zh: 1983年，电子游戏行业崩溃了，对那些当时还没出生的人来说，可能不太了解。

cues.en: What happened was very simply,
cues.zh: 事情其实很简单，

cues.en: what Activision did,
cues.zh: 就是动视做的，

cues.en: as as our questioner
cues.zh: 正如提问者

cues.en: said, opened the floodgates.
cues.zh: 所说，打开了闸门。

cues.en: We were very successful making money hand over fist, and people says, I can do that.
cues.zh: 我们当时赚得盆满钵满，人们就说，我也能做到。

cues.en: And venture capitalists stepped up and started funding these companies to do just what we're doing.
cues.zh: 风险投资家们纷纷涌现，开始资助这些公司做我们正在做的事。

cues.en: But when we were doing it, there were only about,
cues.zh: 但我们做的时候，全世界只有大约

cues.en: you know, 10 people
cues.zh: 你知道，10个人

cues.en: in the world who could do this, who knew what... How to do this. It was very left brain and right brain intensive. You had to be extremely technical and still be creative, and you had to figure out what's fun and all those things.
cues.zh: 能做这个，知道怎么……怎么做。这非常需要左右脑并用。你得技术极强，同时还要有创造力，你得搞清楚什么好玩等等。

cues.en: And they were hiring high school kids who said, yeah, I can program a computer, and so the quality of the games really crashed.
cues.zh: 而他们雇了些高中生，这些人说，是啊，我会编程，结果游戏质量真的一落千丈。

cues.en: I mean, I'm talking about a time when there was no game... No GDC.
cues.zh: 我是说，那时候还没有游戏……没有GDC。

cues.en: The equivalent of GDC was when the Activision game programmers
cues.zh: GDC的等价物就是动视的游戏程序员

cues.zh: 和雅达利的游戏程序员

cues.zh: 在当地商场的food court偶遇。

cues.en: I mean, that was it.
cues.zh: 就是这样。

cues.en: So there wasn't the talent base necessary
cues.zh: 所以当时没有足够的人才基础

cues.en: to do great games.
cues.zh: 来做伟大的游戏。

cues.en: So Venture Capitalist stepped up. They spent $2,000,000
cues.zh: 于是风险投资家们进场了。他们花了200万美元

cues.en: on this company, $2,000,000 on that company. In one six month period,
cues.zh: 投这家公司，200万美元投那家公司。在短短六个月内，

cues.en: 30 companies showed up doing video games that weren't in the brochure at the last trade show,
cues.zh: 30家做电子游戏的公司冒了出来，上次交易会的宣传册上根本没有他们，

cues.en: and we looked at each other and said, the crap they're putting out, they're not gonna be in business a year from now.
cues.zh: 我们互相看了看说，他们出的那些垃圾，一年后肯定就不在了。

cues.en: We were right. We didn't realize when we said that that every one of them going out of business was gonna completely destroy the market,
cues.zh: 我们说得没错。当时我们那么说的时候，并没有意识到，他们每一家倒闭都会彻底摧毁市场，

cues.en: And what happened there was people...
cues.zh: 当时发生的情况是，人们……

cues.en: They had a warehouse full of games and they go out of business, so some liquidator comes in, pays the bankruptcy trustee three bucks apiece to buy them out of the out of the warehouse,
cues.zh: 他们的仓库里堆满了游戏，然后倒闭了，于是清算人进来，按每件三美元的价格向破产受托人买下仓库里的货，

cues.en: retails them... Or wholesales them for $4 and tells the retailer, you can sell these for $5 apiece.
cues.zh: 零售出去……或者以四美元批发出去，告诉零售商，你可以每件五美元卖出去。

cues.en: And those people who were alive for that era, you walked into a Toys R Us or KB Toys, and there was this barrel
cues.zh: 经历过那个时代的人，走进 Toys R Us 或 KB Toys，门口就摆着这么一个大桶，

cues.en: in front of the doors filled with 2,600 cartridges, just random 2,600 cartridges, $5 apiece, $5 apiece.
cues.zh: 里面装满了 2,600 盒卡带，就是随机的 2,600 盒卡带，每盒五美元，每盒五美元。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: the kid tells dad, you know, I want the latest Activision game under the Christmas tree, so... And they're about $40.
cues.zh: 孩子跟爸爸说，你知道，我想在圣诞树下看到最新的 Activision 游戏，所以……它们大概四十美元。

cues.en: Dad walks into KB Toys and says, wait a minute. I can buy eight games for my $40? I'm gonna be a hero.
cues.zh: 爸爸走进 KB Toys 说，等一下。我花四十美元能买八个游戏？我要成英雄了。

cues.en: So in one Christmas, sales of new games went to zero.
cues.zh: 结果一个圣诞节，新游戏的销量就归零了。

cues.en: There were 20,000,000
cues.zh: 市面上有两千万

cues.en: cartridges out there in those barrels that had to sell through first before anything we were doing could be sold as a new game,
cues.zh: 盒卡带堆在那些桶里，必须先卖完这些，我们做的东西才能作为新游戏卖出去，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: it's pretty hard on the on the industry.
cues.zh: 这对整个行业来说相当艰难。

cues.en: As for coming out of it, yes. When we came out of it, Nintendo,
cues.zh: 至于走出困境，是的。当我们走出来的时候，任天堂，

cues.en: the American video game industry was bloody.
cues.zh: 美国电子游戏行业血流成河。

cues.en: Nintendo came in and brought their NES,
cues.zh: 任天堂进来，带来了他们的 NES，

cues.en: but they signed up
cues.zh: 但他们让

cues.en: developers and publishers to a very restrictive contract, and you had to sign that contract if you wanted to do anything for Nintendo,
cues.zh: 开发者和发行商签了一份非常苛刻的合同，如果你想为任天堂做任何事，就必须签那份合同，

cues.en: and then they controlled the business,
cues.zh: 然后他们控制了整个生意，

cues.en: and they got a little heavy handed and caused other problems. So we go through cycles. I mean, we're gonna go through more cycles.
cues.zh: 而且他们有点过于强硬，引发了其他问题。所以我们会经历周期。我是说，我们还会经历更多周期。

cues.zh: 我已经有另一个问题了。你可以先来。当然。

cues.zh: 说到动视的游戏，我首先想到的就是那些经典封面和标志性的彩虹。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.zh: 尤其是Pitfall

cues.en: stood out for a couple reasons.
cues.zh: 它脱颖而出有几个原因。

cues.en: One of them being it most closely resembled the actual game rather than some BS that just made you wanna buy the game. And I was just wondering if you could tell us a little bit about the artist.
cues.zh: 其中一个原因是它最接近实际游戏画面，而不是那种只是为了让你想买游戏的虚假宣传。我想问问你能不能给我们讲讲那位艺术家。

cues.en: Who did that? Was he in house?
cues.zh: 是谁画的？是公司内部的吗？

cues.en: Well, no. It was one of actually... Another one of our founding principles.
cues.zh: 嗯，不是。那其实是……我们的另一个创立原则。

cues.en: Atari, at the time, was doing highly stylized
cues.zh: 当时雅达利做的是高度风格化的

cues.en: box art,
cues.zh: 盒装封面，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: we basically went to our business people, and I said, no. We're not gonna do that. If you want... I I want you to be able to look at the box and decide you wanna buy this game because you're not gonna know until you get it home and plug it into the machine.
cues.zh: 我们直接去找了商务人员，我说，不。我们不做那种。如果你想……我希望你能看着盒子就决定要不要买这个游戏，因为在你拿回家插进机器之前你根本不知道它是什么样。

cues.en: So we insisted on absolute pixel identical
cues.zh: 所以我们坚持要绝对像素级一致的

cues.en: art on the front cover,
cues.zh: 封面画面，

cues.en: and our marketing people looked back and said, you're absolutely out of your mind. No. We're not gonna do that, but we will put a screenshot on the back,
cues.zh: 我们的营销人员回头说，你绝对是疯了。不。我们不会那么做，但我们会在背面放一张截图，

cues.en: and then on the front, we'll do some sort of an artistic rendering of the screenshot,
cues.zh: 然后在正面，我们会对截图做一些艺术化的渲染，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: that's really where that came about.
cues.zh: 这就是那个做法的由来。

cues.zh: 还有一次，我在Jim Levy的办公室里，他是我们选来运营这家公司的人，

cues.en: us programmer guys,
cues.zh: 我们这些程序员，

cues.zh: 他看向架子上摆着一堆雅达利游戏，他说，看看那些。他说，你根本看不出那些游戏是来自同一家公司，

cues.zh: 他对此很有眼光。所以如果你把所有动视的盒子并排堆起来，

cues.zh: 字体是一样的，布局是一样的，你知道，一切都协调

cues.zh: 就像一个家族一样。

cues.zh: 所以我们坚持要有一个游戏，

cues.zh: 你懂的，真正游戏的画面，
